text: The pipeline begins with data collection to assemble a wide dynamic range face dataset across diverse lighting environments.
Raw images of multiple subjects are captured under both artificial and natural lighting setups.
The captured data undergoes postprocessing, including format conversion and channel adjustments.
Images are then classified and filtered to clean the dataset before forwarding to the next stage.
In the tone mapping stage, high dynamic range images are compressed for standard vision algorithms.
Only images with a dynamic range exceeding two to the fifteenth power are retained for the benchmark.
Twenty-five distinct tone mapping operators process the wide dynamic range images.
This produces twenty-five tone-mapped image sets ready for downstream face detection.
The final stage performs face detection across the tone-mapped datasets.
Eight face detectors are deployed across the generated image collections.
Each detector locates faces under extreme backlighting and varying illuminance distributions.
Finally, comprehensive results and analysis determine the impact of tone mapping methods on face detection accuracy.
